chunks.heading: Dental implant lifespan: post vs crown
chunks.content: A dental implant has two parts with different lifespans. The titanium post fused to your jaw is designed to be permanent and, with good care, often lasts for decades or a lifetime. The crown on top takes the daily wear of chewing, so it usually lasts 10 to 15 years before it may need replacing. When people ask about dental implant lifespan, the crown is usually the part that needs attention first.

chunks.placement: New FAQ section before the conclusion
chunks.heading: Dental implant FAQs
chunks.content:
Q: Do dental implants last forever?
A: The implant post can last a lifetime, but the whole implant isn't maintenance-free. The crown usually needs replacing after 10 to 15 years, and gum disease, smoking or teeth grinding can shorten the life of the post. Brushing, flossing and regular check-ups give your implant the best chance of lasting.

chunks.placement: New H2 after 'What affects how long an implant lasts'
chunks.heading: Signs your dental implant may be failing
chunks.content:
See your dentist promptly if you notice any of these dental implant failure signs:
- The implant or crown feels loose or moves when you bite
- Pain or throbbing around the implant that doesn't settle
- Swollen, red or bleeding gums around the implant
- Gum shrinking back so the metal post becomes visible
- Difficulty or discomfort when chewing
Caught early, many implant problems can be treated without losing the implant.

chunks.placement: New H2 before 'Caring for your implant'

chunks.content:

| Typical lifespan | Post: decades; crown: 10-15 years | Typically [10-15] years |
| Effect on nearby teeth | None - stands alone | Neighbouring teeth are filed down to hold it |
| Jawbone | Helps preserve bone | Bone can shrink under the gap |
On implant vs bridge longevity, an implant usually wins because the post can last a lifetime and it doesn't rely on the teeth next to it. A bridge can be a good, quicker option when implants aren't suitable.
